title: The Donkey with the Leopard Spots (HI)
summary: A fraudulent trader paints black spots on a donkey and tries to sell it as a rare hunting beast. Birbal unmasks the painted fraud with a bucket of water. [HI]
full_text:
A dishonest animal dealer from the western provinces arrived in Agra with a bizarre animal: a sturdy four-legged beast covered in bright yellow fur with black circular rosettes, resembling a leopard, yet possessing long ears and hooves!

The trader proclaimed in the animal bazaar: 'Behold, citizens! This is a celestial hunting beast from the Tibetan plateau—the Leopard-Ass! It possesses the speed of a leopard and the endurance of an ass! It can be yours for only five hundred silver rupees!'

Several wealthy nobles were fascinated and on the verge of purchasing the curiosity.

Birbal happened to ride by with Emperor Akbar. Akbar stopped his horse in wonder: 'Birbal, look at that creature! Have you ever heard of a leopard-ass?'

Birbal looked at the animal, noticed the chemical smell of turmeric and lampblack in the air, and smiled: 'Sire, nature creates wondrous creatures, but human deceit creates even more colorful ones.'

Birbal walked to the public fountain, filled a leather bucket with warm soapy water, and walked up to the strange beast.

Before the trader could protest, Birbal dumped the entire bucket of soapy water over the animal's flank!

Thick yellow dye and black ink poured down the animal's legs, pooling into the street gutter. Underneath the washed fur emerged the ordinary, dull grey coat of a common village donkey!

The donkey shook its wet ears, puffed its snout, and brayed loudly: *Hee-haw! Hee-haw!*

The crowd burst into uproarious laughter, while the fraudulent trader fell to his knees in terror.

Birbal said to Emperor Akbar: 'You see, Your Majesty? A crook may paint leopard spots upon a donkey, and fools may admire the decoration. But a single splash of honest water washes away the paint, and the beast brayed with its true voice.'

Akbar ordered the swindler fined and banished, commending Birbal for washing away deceit with common sense.
